title: Calendar Whiplash
blurb: History's timeline, but somebody shuffled it. Three are real. One is cap.

cards.say: [Betty White was born before sliced bread was first sold], [the first lighter was invented before the friction match], [Queen Victoria was still reigning when the Wright brothers flew], and [Genghis Khan was still alive when the Magna Carta was sealed].
cards.real: Queen Victoria died in January 1901, almost three years before the Wright brothers' first flight in December 1903.

cards.say: [Charles Dickens lived long enough to see the telephone patented], [Harriet Tubman lived long enough to see the Wright brothers fly], [Orville Wright lived long enough to see a plane break the sound barrier], and [Ben Franklin lived long enough to see George Washington become president].
cards.real: Dickens died in 1870, six years before Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (Bell's March 1876 patent confirmed; Dickens's 1870 death is textbook) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Graham_Bell
NOT WEB-CHECKED (Washington's April 30, 1789 inauguration confirmed; Franklin's April 1790 death is textbook) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington

cards.say: [Marilyn Monroe and Queen Elizabeth II were born in the same year], [Galileo was born the same week that Michelangelo died], [Bach and Handel were born in the same year and never once met], and [Shakespeare and Cervantes were born in the same year].
cards.real: Cervantes was born in 1547, 17 years before Shakespeare. The pair did die in the same year, 1616.

cards.say: [The Eastern Roman Empire still existed when the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan], [the Eiffel Tower was completed three years before the Statue of Liberty], [Ireland's Newgrange tomb is older than the Great Pyramid of Giza], and [Vikings were in Newfoundland 471 years before Columbus crossed the Atlantic].
cards.real: The Statue of Liberty was dedicated in 1886, three years before the Eiffel Tower opened in 1889. Gustave Eiffel even engineered the statue's iron frame.

cards.say: [A movie was streamed over the internet before Netflix was even founded], [Facebook was up and running before LinkedIn launched], [the Soviet Union still existed when the first website went online], and [the PlayStation 2 was still being made five years after the PS3 came out].
cards.real: LinkedIn launched in May 2003. Facebook didn't launch until February 2004.

cards.say: [China's last emperor was still alive for the first Super Bowl], [President John Tyler, born in 1790, had a grandson alive in 2024], [the US government was still paying a Civil War pension in 2020], and [Napoleon was still alive when Queen Victoria took the throne].
cards.real: Napoleon died in 1821, 16 years before Victoria became queen in 1837.

cards.say: [The first Ferris wheel was built for the same fair as the Eiffel Tower], [Dr Pepper was being served in Texas before Coca-Cola existed], [the oldest recording of a human voice is older than the phonograph], and [the classic Nokia ringtone comes from a guitar piece written in 1902].
cards.real: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 Paris fair. The first Ferris wheel was Chicago's answer to it, at the 1893 World's Fair.

cards.say: [The last independent Maya kingdom fell after Newton published his laws of motion], [work on Neuschwanstein Castle began after the American Civil War ended], [Machu Picchu was already built when work began on Notre-Dame in Paris], and [Hawaii's royal palace had electric lights before the White House did].
cards.real: Work on Notre-Dame began in 1163. Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the mid-1400s, almost three centuries later.

cards.say: [Woodstock happened less than a month after the Moon landing], [the first email was sent two years after the first cellphone call], [Apple was founded before the first Star Wars movie came out], and [NBA games had no three-point line until 1979].
cards.real: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971, two years before Martin Cooper made the first handheld cellphone call in 1973.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Moon landing July 20, 1969; Woodstock August 15-18, 1969) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock
NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: the NBA adopted the three-point line for the 1979-80 season) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-point_field_goal

cards.say: [Queen Elizabeth II's first prime minister was born in 1874], [King Tut's tomb was found the same year the BBC began broadcasting], [Greece didn't switch to the modern calendar until 1923], and [Russia's October Revolution actually took place in September].
cards.real: Russia still used the old Julian calendar, so the revolution's October 25 was November 7 everywhere else. It was late, not early.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Churchill, born 1874, was prime minister at Elizabeth II's 1952 accession) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill

cards.say: [The Battle of New Orleans came after the War of 1812 peace treaty was signed], [the Hundred Years' War between England and France lasted 116 years], [Concorde was still flying passengers when the first iPhone came out], and [the original VW Beetle was still being built in Mexico in 2003].
cards.real: Concorde's last passenger flight was in October 2003, almost four years before the first iPhone went on sale in June 2007.

cards.say: [England's first flushing toilet was built for Queen Victoria], [the first known written OMG was in a 1917 letter to Winston Churchill], [the word meme was coined in 1976, long before the World Wide Web], and [Santa Fe, New Mexico was founded before the Pilgrims reached Plymouth].
cards.real: Sir John Harington built a flushing toilet for Queen Elizabeth I around 1596, more than 200 years before Victoria was born.
